page: Amazon Web Services c5d.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine is powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor clocked at 3.4 GHz under the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, representing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA. Graphics acceleration is absent with 0 GPUs available. Local storage is provided through an integrated 100 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results show moderate performance in single-threaded tasks and lower relative standing in multi-core metrics. The instance achieved 24.03 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 9.13 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. In Geekbench testing, the c5d.xlarge scored 1142.0 on single-core and 2507.0 on multi-core execution, with software compilation reaching 3555.0. Stress-ng returned 1405.09 for single-core and 3692.85 for multi-core performance. PassMark evaluations yielded a CPU score of 4426.46 and a memory score of 1073.65. Network and cache throughput measures recorded 3.65 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.94 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bundled 100 GB NVMe SSD offers high-throughput, low-latency disk I/O without incurring external volume attachments, though data is ephemeral. The 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation and 1 Gbps baseline network capacity restrict the instance from handling heavy memory footprints or bandwidth-intensive data movement. As a result, the c5d.xlarge is suited for localized continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data transformations, web applications requiring fast scratch disks, and temporary caching layers.
